chunks: From him, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus ibn Abdillah, from Ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about men who shared in a slave-girl, and they entrusted one of them so that the slave-girl would be with him, and he had intercourse with her. He said: 'The fine is deferred from him according to the value of his share in her in cash, and he is whipped according to what is not his share in her. The slave-girl is valued for him at a price, and he is bound to her. If the valuation is less than the price at which the girl was bought, he is bound to pay her first price. And if her valuation on that day on which she was valued is more than her price, he is bound to that price. And he is small (liable for the lesser share) because he had intercourse with her.' I said: 'If one of the partners wishes to buy her without the man, he said: 'That is for him, and it is not for him to buy her until she is cleared (of pregnancy), and it is not upon the other to buy her except at the valuation.'

I said: 'If one of the partners wishes to buy her without the man,' he said: 'That is for him, and it is not for him to buy her until she is cleared (of pregnancy), and it is not upon the other to buy her except at the valuation.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial and legal consequences when one partner in a shared slave-girl has intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the jurisprudence of *Istibra* (waiting period) and financial liability when co-owners of a female slave share in her sexual rights, specifically addressing how the *hadd* penalty is apportioned according to each partner's share. It further clarifies the valuation mechanism for compensation, ensuring that the partner who exercised his right bears the cost, while other partners retain the option to purchase her share only after she is free from pregnancy. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise equity in shared property rights and the procedural safeguards against premature sale.
